$comment: PKG-1 core-app quiesce ordering (contracts.md#pkg-1--core-app-quiesce), for release-managed content replaced under Leaf's own control (OTA payload swap, make stage-app). Same fixture shape as txn1-ordering.json so B4a's tests can share a runner.

steps.name: snapshot-desired-and-effective-state
steps.action: Snapshot desired and effective state for every service.
steps.if_crash_here: Nothing changed; a fresh operation re-snapshots.

steps.name: stop-and-verify
steps.action: Stop every affected service with the SVC-1 stop sequence; verify absence.
steps.if_crash_here: An unverified stop, or a still-locked stale-generation lease, fails the operation outright. Bytes are never changed under a live process.

steps.name: block-new-starts
steps.action: Block new service starts and package-owned foreground launches for the duration.
steps.if_crash_here: Block is process-lifetime state; a crash here simply ends the operation before step 4, no payload touched.

steps.name: replace-payload
steps.action: Replace the payload. Atomicity of the payload swap itself belongs to Leaf's updater (or the stage-app script for development), not to PKG-1.
steps.if_crash_here: Recovery is the updater's own responsibility -- PKG-1 has no journal and no rollback sibling of its own.

steps.name: rescan-and-restore
steps.action: Rescan manifests; restore desired state; start services whose desired intent is enabled and whose manifest still validates.
steps.if_crash_here: Re-running rescan-and-restore is idempotent: it starts exactly the services whose desired intent is enabled and whose manifest currently validates, regardless of how many times it is interrupted and re-run.

invariant: Step 2's verified absence is the only thing that licenses step 4. There is no journal because the updater owns payload atomicity; PKG-1's contribution is purely the quiesce/restore bracket around it.
